chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about four men who testified against a man for adultery, and when he was killed, one of them withdrew his testimony. He said: 'The one who withdraws is killed, and the remaining three pay to his family three-quarters of the blood money.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation and penalty for witnesses in an adultery case if one withdraws testimony after execution?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *qisas* (retaliatory justice) applied to witnesses in cases of capital punishment, specifically addressing the scenario where one of four witnesses retracts testimony post-execution. According to this ruling, the retracting witness faces death for the wrongful execution, while the remaining three bear financial liability for the remaining three-quarters of the blood money (*diyah*). This highlights the high stakes of judicial testimony in Shia fiqh, ensuring accountability for both the act of testifying and the accuracy of that testimony.
